Pixel-by-Pixel Cube Fitting

Fit a Gaussian to the spectrum of every spatial pixel in the cube, producing 2D parameter maps that show how the line properties vary across the field.

This is the full-cube counterpart to 1D Spectrum Fitting. The per-pixel fit is the same algorithm, but the workflow, the required inputs and the outputs are different: a noise region becomes mandatory, non-detections are turned into upper limits rather than discarded, and the result is a set of maps rather than a single number per parameter.

Note

Fit the 1D spectrum first. Run 1D Spectrum Fitting on a representative pixel or region before starting a cube fit. That is how you find a sensible wavelength window and confirm the line is actually there. A full-cube run over a badly chosen window takes minutes and produces maps of noise.

Setting Up the Fit

The cube fit reuses the same toggle buttons as the 1D fit, but requires a different subset of them.

Wavelength window (required)

Set Left and Right to bracket the line. These become the fit window for every pixel.

Peak is not required. Unlike the 1D fit, the cube fit does not use your λ_peak click. Instead it fits the summed spectrum of the whole cube once to derive initial guesses, and if a HITRAN line list is loaded it will use the nearest catalog line in the window as the center seed. This “global 1D fit” is reported back to you in the results window.

Noise region (required)

Set Noise L and Noise R over a line-free stretch of spectrum. The cube fit refuses to start without them — you will get a “Noise Region Required” warning.

Unlike the 1D fit — where a noise region is only demanded for very narrow windows, and does not affect the result even then (see The Noise Region) — here it is always required and it directly shapes the output.

The noise region is not optional decoration here. The standard deviation measured in it sets the detection threshold: a pixel counts as a detection when its fitted amplitude exceeds 3σ of the noise and the fit improves on the residuals. Everything else is recorded as an upper limit. Choose a region close in wavelength to the line, and genuinely free of features — a noise region that clips a line wing inflates σ and silently demotes real detections to upper limits.

Running the Fit

  1. Click Fit Gaussian Map

  2. Confirm at the “Continue with map fitting?” prompt

  3. The fit runs on 8 worker threads in the background

Watching progress. The dialog that appears is an indeterminate busy indicator — it does not show a percentage, and the “Hide” button dismisses it without cancelling the run. Actual progress is printed to the console you launched the application from:

Fitting Gaussians to 122500 pixels in wavelength range [6.9000, 6.9500]
Using 8 worker threads (122,500 pixels)
  Progress: 12250/122500 pixels (10.0%)
  Progress: 24500/122500 pixels (20.0%)
  ...
Fitting complete: 98211/122500 successful fits (80.2%)
  Detections (>3.0 sigma): 41022 (33.5%)
  Upper limits: 57189 (46.7%)

If the window appears frozen, check the console — that is where liveness shows up.

Results are cached. Re-running with the same Left/Right and the same Noise L/Noise R reuses the previous fit instead of recomputing it, and tells you so. Change any of the four boundaries to force a fresh run.

Reading the Results

The results window opens automatically when the fit completes, headed by a summary:

  • Successfully fit N / M pixels — how many converged at all

  • Detections | Upper limits — the 3σ split described above

  • Global 1D fit — the summed-spectrum fit used to seed the per-pixel initial guesses, and where its center came from

Below that, a dropdown selects which map to display, with colormap and scale controls (Linear, Log, or Percentile 2–98%).

Output Maps

Available in the dropdown:

Map

Contents

Area (AUC)

Integrated line flux per pixel, A × σ × √(2π). In erg/s/cm² for MIRI, NIRSpec and MUSE (see the unit table on the 1D page); otherwise in the cube’s native flux×wavelength units.

Amplitude

Peak height above the baseline, converted to CGS where the header allows it

Center

Fitted line center wavelength — this is your velocity map, once converted

Sigma

Gaussian σ, in the spectral axis unit

FWHM

2.355 × σ

chi2 (fit quality)

Reduced chi-squared per pixel. χ²_red ≈ 1 is a good fit, >> 1 is poor, << 1 means overfitting. This is a real χ² — it exists here, and not in the 1D fit, precisely because the mandatory noise region supplies the σ it needs.

Success Mask

Binary map of which pixels converged

Residuals

Data minus fitted model. Display only — see the export note below.

Upper limits

For pixels that fail the detection threshold the area is not set to NaN. It is replaced with a 1σ upper limit, std_residuals × σ_guess × √(2π), and the pixel is flagged in the is_upper_limit mask.

This matters downstream: Rotational Diagram detects censored points and switches from ordinary least squares to Bayesian censored regression rather than discarding them. Failed fits — as opposed to non-detections — do store NaN.

Exporting Maps as FITS

With a map selected in the dropdown, click Save as FITS File. Each map is written as a single-slice FITS file you can reopen in the 2D viewer (2D FITS Dual Image Viewer) or in external tools.

Warning

Residuals cannot be exported from this dialog. It appears in the display dropdown but not in the export list, so choosing it and clicking save produces a “Cannot export” warning. To get residuals to disk, use export_residual_cube from the API (below), which writes the full 3D residual cube.

Using the API

Fitting the cube

from cube_explorer.api import load_cube, create_gaussian_map

cube = load_cube("data.fits")

maps = create_gaussian_map(
    cube,
    lam_min=6.90,
    lam_max=6.95,
    noise_min=7.00,        # Line-free region, as in the GUI
    noise_max=7.05,
    fac_above_stdres=3.0,  # Detection threshold in sigma
    n_jobs=8,
)

print(f"Converged:    {maps['success'].sum()}")
print(f"Detections:   {maps['is_detection'].sum()}")
print(f"Upper limits: {maps['is_upper_limit'].sum()}")

area_map = maps['area']          # 2D array, shape (n_y, n_x)

Important

fac_above_stdres defaults to 2.0 in the API but the GUI passes 3.0. If you are trying to reproduce a GUI result in a script, set it to 3.0 explicitly — otherwise you will get more detections than the GUI reported for the same cube.

n_jobs defaults to auto-detected CPU count in the API; the GUI hardcodes 8.

Returned keys

maps['amplitude']         # Peak amplitude, CGS where available
maps['amp_originalunits'] # Peak amplitude in the cube's own units
maps['center']            # Line center wavelength
maps['sigma']             # Gaussian sigma
maps['fwhm']              # 2.355 * sigma
maps['area']              # Integrated flux (or 1-sigma upper limit)
maps['r_squared']         # SEE WARNING BELOW - this is reduced chi-squared
maps['success']           # Boolean: did the fit converge?
maps['is_detection']      # Boolean: passed the sigma threshold
maps['is_upper_limit']    # Boolean: area is a 1-sigma upper limit
maps['residuals_cube']    # 3D residuals cached during fitting
maps['fac_above_stdres']  # The threshold that was used
maps['wavelength_unit']   # Spectral axis unit string
maps['global_fit']        # The summed-spectrum fit used for initial guesses

Danger

The key 'r_squared' does not contain R². It holds the reduced chi-squared map — the same values the GUI correctly labels “chi2 (fit quality)”. The key name is a historical misnomer.

Interpret it as χ²_red: near 1 is good, large is bad. Code that treats it like R² and keeps pixels above some threshold will select the worst fits in the cube.

Exporting a residual cube

Fits and subtracts a Gaussian at every pixel, writing the normalized residuals to a 3D FITS file:

from cube_explorer.api import load_cube, export_residual_cube

cube = load_cube("data.fits")

export_residual_cube(
    cube,
    out_path="residual.fits",
    lam_min=6.90,
    lam_max=6.95,
)

# Or keep the array in memory as well
path, residuals = export_residual_cube(
    cube, out_path="residual.fits",
    lam_min=6.90, lam_max=6.95, return_cube=True,
)

Constraints and Tips

  1. Left < Right, and the noise region must be set — the run will not start otherwise

  2. Keep the noise region close in wavelength to the fit window. Detector noise varies with wavelength, so a distant noise estimate misstates the detection threshold across the whole map

  3. Keep the fit window tight. Every extra wavelength sample is fitted for every pixel, so a window twice as wide costs roughly twice the runtime and degrades χ²_red

  4. Always check the Success Mask and the detection/upper-limit counts before interpreting a parameter map. A beautiful-looking area map built from 15% converged pixels is mostly interpolated nothing

  5. Use the chi2 map to find where the model breaks down — blended lines and P-Cygni-like profiles show up as coherent high-χ² structure, not as scattered noise
